notes: Guided first-run setup (Guide.kt). Each answer adds categories with a description sentence and a base: a typical monthly amount in dollars for one person. Household multiplies the bases (per category, '*' for the rest). Suggested budgets follow the money available: spending grows slower than income (spending_vs_income), and each category grows with spending at its own rate (elasticity: 0 = a fixed need, 1 = in step, above 1 = grows faster). budget = base x household x ((money for spending / sum of bases) ^ spending_vs_income) ^ elasticity, scaled down together if it doesn't fit; what's left over is suggested as savings. Calibrated to the BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024 (see 'calibration'). Edit freely: nothing about these categories is in code. Goals: each one ticked becomes its own category, budgeted at its monthly amount; 'absorbs' names a spending category the goal replaces (a trip goal takes over Travel: its description, keywords and the purchases).

calibration.source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024: Table 1101 (quintiles of income before taxes) and the size-of-consumer-unit table, bls.gov/cex/tables.htm
calibration.spending_vs_income: Total spending vs income before taxes across income quintiles: log-log slope 0.53 (bottom fifth earns $16.7k and spends $35.0k a year, top fifth $264.5k and $150.3k).
calibration.elasticity: Each category's spending per person vs total spending per person across income quintiles, log-log slope. groceries = food at home 0.28; dining = food away 1.09; transportation = gasoline 0.49, other vehicle 0.83, public transport 1.55 (0.6 blended); fun = entertainment 1.35; shopping = apparel 0.80; subscriptions = audio/visual 0.29; fitness = fees and admissions 2.46 (1.5: that line also holds tickets); hobbies = entertainment 1.35; health = healthcare 0.45 and personal care 0.93 (0.6 blended); pets 1.23; miscellaneous 1.0 (by definition). Not in the tables, estimated: kids 1.0, travel 1.5.
calibration.household: Two-person vs one-person households: food at home 1.79, food away 1.81, apparel 1.79, entertainment 1.80, healthcare 1.80, gasoline 1.92, other vehicle 1.80, audio/visual 1.52, fees and admissions 2.15, pets 2.03. Four-person vs one: food at home 2.56, food away 2.60, apparel 2.38, entertainment 2.28, healthcare 1.89, gasoline 2.84, other vehicle 2.57, audio/visual 1.43, pets 1.96. Larger households also earn more, so these overstate need somewhat.
calibration.base: One-person households average a month: food at home $283, food away $187, entertainment $182, apparel $93, gasoline $112, public transport $61, audio/visual $61, personal care $52, pets $42 (owners or not). The bases are close to these.

questions.text: Do you spend regularly on any of these?

Things for hobbies: games, books, music, craft supplies and gear.
Looking after yourself: pharmacy, copays, haircuts and personal care products.
The pet: food, supplies, grooming and vet visits.
Trips away from home: flights, hotels and rentals, rental cars and long-distance trains. Meals on a trip go here too.
